effective.basis: Old state: UDE official card rulings (Sangan/Witch: 'If you have no eligible monsters, your opponent gets to see your Deck to verify', captured 2005-06-16) through Konami's own per-set rulings documents - Machina Mayhem (2010-04-06, 18 days before the Edison snapshot), Starstrike Blast (2010-11-16), Storm of Ragnarok (2011-02-02). New state: KDE-US Tournament Policy section 'Card/Hand/Deck Verification' forbids verifying the opponent's Deck (first located capture 2019-04-03; still current in v2.5, 2025-09-05). No dated announcement of the change was found, so the interval 2011-02-02 .. 2019-04-03 stays open.

corroboration.title: UDE official Yu-Gi-Oh! Card Rulings (capture 2005-06-16, inside the GOAT window)
corroboration.quote: You must show your opponent the monster you select from your Deck for this card's effect. If you have no eligible monsters, your opponent gets to see your Deck to verify.

corroboration.title: Konami, Machina Mayhem Structure Deck Card Rulings, compiled April 6th 2010 (18 days before the Edison snapshot)
corroboration.quote: If you do not have "Commander Covington" in your Deck, your opponent can ask to verify.

corroboration.title: Konami, Storm of Ragnarok Card Rulings, compiled February 2 2011 - the latest positive attestation of the old state
corroboration.quote: If there is no longer a monster in your hand that you can Special Summon when this effect resolves, your opponent may briefly verify that this is the case.

changes.historical_text: If this card attacks a face-down Defense Position monster, destroy the monster immediately with this card's effect without flipping it face-up or applying damage calculation. During the End Phase of a turn that this card destroyed a monster as a result of battle, send this card to the Graveyard to Special Summon 1 "Mystic Swordsman LV4" from your hand or Deck.
changes.summary: Period procedure, not a text erratum: if the End Phase effect resolves and no 'Mystic Swordsman LV4' is in the hand or Deck, the goat script reveals both zones (Duel.GoatConfirm(tp,LOCATION_HAND+LOCATION_DECK)); the modern script has no reveal branch. No lineage version prints reveal wording.

changes.historical_text: If this card attacks a face-down Defense Position monster, destroy the monster immediately with this card's effect without flipping it face-up or applying damage calculation. During the End Phase of a turn that this card destroyed a monster as a result of battle, send this card to the Graveyard to Special Summon 1 "Mystic Swordsman LV4" from your hand or Deck.
changes.summary: Separate per-card era allowance: the goat sptg is `if chk==0 then return ft>0 end` where the modern sptg also requires `Duel.IsExistingMatchingCard(s.spfilter,tp,LOCATION_HAND|LOCATION_DECK,0,1,nil,e,tp)`. In the period implementation the End Phase effect can therefore be activated and its cost paid - this card is sent to the Graveyard - with no LV4 anywhere to Summon, spending the monster for nothing; modern rules forbid the activation outright. No source dates when this card lost that allowance.

review.notes: The remaining script differences are verified non-behavioural: the goat local s.spcost is byte-equivalent to the modern library's Cost.SelfToGrave (cardscripts/utility.lua:1434-1438, same IsAbleToGraveAsCost check and SendtoGrave(REASON_COST)); s.LVset=0x5f is the numeric value of SET_MYSTIC_SWORDSMAN; and RESET_EVENT+RESETS_STANDARD+RESET_PHASE+PHASE_END is the expansion of RESETS_STANDARD_PHASE_END (cardscripts/constant.lua:300). Text lineage v0 (SOD-EN011, 2004-10-01) -> v1 (SD5-EN013, 2005-11-02) -> v2 (DR3-EN011, 2006-11-25) -> v3 (LCYW-EN200, 2012-09-29) is PSCT formalisation of the same resolution: 'destroy the monster immediately ... without flipping it face-up or applying damage calculation' becomes 'At the start of the Damage Step ...: Destroy that monster', which both scripts already implement as an EVENT_BATTLE_START trigger; 'send this face-up card to the Graveyard' adds no face-up check in either script. Intermediate-state reasoning as for the other GoatConfirm cards: the two ruling transitions are unordered, no upstream implementation covers the state between them, and none is attached because GOAT (2005-04-01) and Edison (2010-04-24) both precede 2011-02-02.
